physical_context: On the scored observations, A emptied the cup and B refilled it. Derek reported that a pump had fallen at an unknown point. The rate change has no isolated physical cause in these observations. The gap-1b-002-post camera window already shows the rearranged tubes. The full gap-1b journal is retained as a transition record and contributes no dose, error or timing estimate in this cohort. Rewired confirmation and validation use separate records.

camera_transition.interpretation: Dry-region appearance in the one-second bins changed after the last scored pause result. The pump fall and wiring change lack independent timestamps.

method.eligible: Only the qualification, randomized width and pause journals are read. Frozen optical-volume predictions must precede command transmission and match the earlier archive model to journal rounding. Relocations, blanks and interrupted attempts are reported separately.
method.sign: Positive transfer is withdrawal on A or refill on B. Positive error means the model predicted more than the observed delivery. Positive null-minus-prior absolute error favors the pause-sensitive forecast.
method.precision: The primary volume is the mean of the two printed-cup sightlines. Individual sightline changes are in the trial CSV. Camera blanks use the observed signed change in cup level. Vessel graduation tolerance is unknown.
method.groups: Width qualification indexes the first shot on each head after an approximately hour-long idle. Each completed trial contributes one settled dose. Block-level contrasts keep repeats and head direction together and report differences in starting fill. Numbers following a block designate the planned filling/order block; filename suffixes retain retries.
method.timing: Actual timing is measured from host command and receipt times. The first gap estimate uses completion receipt to next start receipt. A second subtracts board-reported on-time from consecutive host writes. The board reports on-time in integer milliseconds.
method.uncertainty: Ranges and sample SD describe the observed trial or matched-block variation. Different initial fills, the same two heads and shared cup calibration limit inference to this apparatus. The pulses and the sightlines within a train are not experimental replicates.
